```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Pain and willingness to pay are both evidenced and high. Reddit users describe expat tax filing as a 'nightmare' and report accountant quotes of $800-$2,500. Sourced self-serve prices run $119-$799, so a single sale at $150-$300 justifies paid acquisition even at a Finance-vertical CPL above the $27.66 average.",
    "A sourced solo-founder precedent exists in the same niche. The brief cites Atamatax as built solo and charging $199-$799 for PFIC-focused self-serve filing. That is direct evidence that one person can ship and sell a narrow version of this product.",
    "Idea B's demand evidence argues against it. Every quote is a complaint about price, in a category where RSS.com offers a free-forever tier and Libsyn starts at $5/month. The pain is already met by cheap or free options, which leaves no clear reason for a podcaster to pay a new entrant.",
    "Idea B adds structural headwinds the brief itself admits. It has low ARPU ($5-$20/month), carries storage, bandwidth and CDN costs, needs feeds that never break, and faces high switching friction from feed-migration fear. All of these slow a first paying customer even though the build is simple.",
    "Idea A's main risks can be scoped down, and Idea B's cannot. Narrowing A to one country pairing, or to a PFIC/FBAR-heavy US-side wedge, avoids the multi-jurisdiction liability problem. B's problems of commoditization and free-tier competition are built into the category."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's acquisition-channel figures (Google CPC $2-$3, Meta CPC $0.26-$0.50, $100-$500/month for 'solid results') come from an RSS.com blog about buying ads to promote a podcast to listeners. They are not costs for acquiring paying hosting subscribers. CPC is also not cost per conversion, so B has no real evidence of what one paying customer costs, especially against free-tier competitors.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Idea A carries serious unresolved risks in the brief. The stated differentiator, local-country filing, is the 'hard part' no competitor has solved. IRS EFIN approval and annual software acceptance testing have unknown timelines that could block e-filing within 90 days. The legality of making country-specific tax calls without licensed local advisors is also open. If the founder insists on the full US-plus-local scope, A's 90-day odds drop sharply. Idea B has lighter regulation and a buildable product but weak evidence that anyone would switch or pay. A wins on stronger demand and pricing evidence, not on ease of execution."
}
```
